sources.citation: Liu, Wen, You-Jing Lin, Zhenghui Yang & Jiangping Kong. 2020 [online 4 Dec 2018]. Hmu (Xinzhai variety). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 50(2): 240-257. doi:10.1017/S0025100318000336 (open access).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress/prosody paragraph at all. Sections: Consonants, Vowels, Tones (8 tones incl. five level tones; breathy voice on /11/; 'tone sandhi is not observed in Hmu'), Syllable structure ('obligatory nucleus (V) on a specific tone'; 'phonologically monosyllabic with a strong tendency towards disyllabicity in its lexicon. Multi-syllabic words are mostly compounds'). Word 'stress' occurs only in a cited reference title.

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien language history. Pacific Linguistics 613. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level only: p.199 (sec. 4.2.1) Hmong-Mien nominal prefixes 'are unstressed, and in some languages they may harmonize with the nouns to which they are attached (Chen 1993)'; p.28 quotes Downer on iambic rhythm in Mien (not Hmongic). Nothing specific to Hmu word stress.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress; instrumental study of the 8 tones (44 51 55 22 45 33 13 11) and phonation on isolated monosyllables; notes the site is Li Fang-kuei's 1940s Black Miao village and that Kwan 1966 partially reports Li's transcriptions.

sources.citation: Mills, Carl & David Strecker. 1988. Diphthongization, syllable structure, and the feature [high] in Hmu. Kansas Working Papers in Linguistics 13: 92-105. doi:10.17161/kwpl.1808.628.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; segmental analysis of Yanghao rhymes (data from Wang Fushi 1979); note 5 lists the eight Yanghao tones and says 'Tones play no part in the problem discussed'.

sources.citation: Wang Fushi 王辅世 (主编). 1985. 苗语简志 Miaoyu jianzhi [A sketch of the Miao language]. 中国少数民族语言简志丛书. Beijing: 民族出版社. 2+203 pp. (Yanghao 养蒿, Kaili = representative of Qiandong/Northern Hmu, pp. 13-16; general remarks p. 3)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for Yanghao/Hmu. p.3: every syllable has a tone that distinguishes meaning; Yanghao section (pp.13-16) gives initials, rhymes, 8 tones (33 55 35 11 44 13 53 31), allophony; no 重音/轻声/轻读 remark for Yanghao (the book's only 轻声 remark, p.12, is about Layiping = Western Xong prefixes qo35/ta35/te35). Ch'ien-tung (Qiandong) is said to lack tone sandhi.

sources.citation: Purnell, Herbert C., Jr. (ed.). 1972. Miao and Yao linguistic studies: selected articles in Chinese, translated by Chang Yü-hung and Chu Kwo-ray. Linguistics Series V, Data Paper 88. Ithaca: Cornell University Southeast Asia Program (contains Miao Language Team 1962 'A brief description of the Miao language'; Ma & T'ai 1936; Ts'ao 1961; P'an & Ts'ao on Eastern Kweichow Miao).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress (the word does not occur). Brief Description p.5: 'Every syllable has a specific tone which serves to distinguish lexical meaning'; 'With the exception of the Ch'ien tung dialect.. all types of Miao have tone sandhi' (i.e., Qiandong/Yanghao lacks sandhi).
